newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in thin trading getting closer to the lower range of the band, dealers said.
The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the market believes the central bank would intervene by buying foreign currency.
"Trading was very quiet today and the volume was low. Despite this, the shekel continued to rise and the basket was traded today at only 6.98 percent below the slope," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The shekel is very close to the lower edge of the band and the Bank of Israel will soon have to intervene," she said.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1370 against 3.1410 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5385 shekels against 3.5402 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9104 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9110 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1266 shekels per mark against 2.1244 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1390 shekels.
